title: Bruce Springsteen Jokes About G-Spots (for a Good Cause) at 2026 Stand Up for Heroes Benefit: 5 Best Moments
summary: The fundraiser for veterans and their families also featured Alex Warren, Jon Stewart and more.
contentText:
For the 20th year in a row, the Bob Woodruff Foundation and the New York Comedy Festival joined forces to raise money — and laughs — for United States veterans, hosting its annual Stand Up for Heroes benefit on Monday (Nov. 9) with performances from Bruce Springsteen , Alex Warren and more.

Held at the David Geffen Hall at the Lincoln Center in New York City, the 2026 fundraiser continued its tradition of supporting former members of the military by bringing many of them, as well as a number of influential figures and donors, into the same room for a night of songs and comedy. The latter was provided this year by longtime supporter of the cause Jon Stewart alongside Josh Johnson and Hasan Minhaj, while the TikToker-turned-singer behind the Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 hit “Ordinary” and The Resilient — a rock band primarily made up of wounded U.S. combat veterans — led the musical offerings.

As for The Boss? He delivered both. Springsteen — who has been present at almost every SUFH since it began in 2007 — sang an intimate handful of tender acoustic cuts as well as blessed the crowd with numerous naughty witticisms.

By the end of the night, founders Bob and Lee Woodruff revealed that they’d raised $5.9 million through the event alone — a number that more than quintupled when billionaire Craigslist founder Craig Newmark, a longtime SUFH supporter and sponsor, announced that he’d be adding $28 million of his own money to the cause. “I like round numbers,” he said with a shrug, revealing that the donation had brought his lifetime contributions to the foundation to an even $100 million.

“You motherf–kers wouldn’t even raise your paddles for $1,000!” Stewart then quipped good-naturedly to the audience.

Though the night’s full programming was reserved only for the honored guests in attendance with a no-cameras policy, Billboard was on site to capture some of the best moments for those who missed out. Keep reading to see the highlights of the 2026 event championing real-life heroes below.
